metadata.description: What changed between two declared versions of the product, translated into the pages somebody has to update (PROP-057 `##OBS-SURFACE-SNAPSHOTS`). `vibe doc diff <old> <new>` compares two surface snapshots member by member and then, through the citation graph, the `derived` sources and the coverage map, names the pages each change reaches and why. A change no page answers to becomes a request for a NEW page rather than silence; an empty document is an answer too. It is the documentation developers' kitchen and nothing of it reaches a reader: the human changelog between versions is written by hand from this output (`##OBS-NOTHING-LEAKS`). Source of truth for `crates/vibe-wire/src/generated/doc_surface_diff/`.
The version number of the older snapshot, as its own file declares it.
The version number of the newer snapshot.
Every difference between the two surfaces, in a stable order: by kind, then by subject.
The pages to update, each with the reasons that reached it. This is the whole point of the document: a writer updates what is listed here instead of re-reading the manual.
Changes no page answers to. They are listed rather than dropped, because «nothing cites the new command» is the state a new page exists to end.
One difference between the two surfaces.
What changed, named the way the surface names it — `vibe doc build`, `vibe doc build --format`, `package.title`, `doc-manifest`, `PROP-057#CARD-FIELDS`.
What about it changed, in one line. Empty for a plain addition or removal, where the subject already says everything.
Which half of the surface the change sits in. Closed because the snapshot has exactly these halves: a kind nobody records cannot change.
Whether the subject appeared, vanished, or stayed and differs.
One page and why the diff reached it.
The page's address inside the documentation package — `reference/cli.xml`.
A change with no page behind it.
